column1: # ZAP runs weekly against the live site from a GitHub-hosted runner
# (.github/workflows/dast.yaml). Findings go to code scanning as SARIF, never to
# the public log, an issue or an artifact.
# WHAT GATES: any HIGH alert, by count (scripts/zap_sarif.py, then the gate
# step). The accepted baseline is zero HIGH. A HIGH that is accepted gets an
# IGNORE row below with its reason, scoped to its host, and an expiry date;
# IGNORE rows are dropped before the count, so every HIGH that reaches the gate
# is new. From the expiry date on the alert counts again: review it, then
# extend or fix. Medium and below report only. FAIL rows are not used: the
# Security headers are gated by scripts/tls-check.sh (STRICT_HEADERS=1 in
# dast.yaml), not by ZAP: the Gateway sets them per route
# (docs/networking.md, Security headers). The header rows below stay WARN so
# ZAP keeps reporting pages an app serves without them.
# Only rules with a stated reason belong here. Everything not listed keeps its
# default behaviour, which for a baseline scan is WARN.
# Find a rule ID in the ZAP HTML report, or:
# Expected because every target sits behind Keycloak
